page: The Vultr vbm-8c-132gb-v2 is a bare-metal server in the Bare Metal NVMe family, designed without virtualization overhead to deliver direct access to physical hardware. It is driven by an Intel Xeon E-2388G processor featuring 8 physical cores and 16 execution threads operating at a base clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture incorporates 48 KB L1 instruction/data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache, alongside specialized instruction sets including AVX-512, AES, and SHA extensions.

Memory capacity is configured with 128.0 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of memory per hardware thread. Storage is provisioned via an integrated 3840 GB NVMe SSD, providing high-capacity, low-latency persistent disk operations. The system does not include dedicated graphics processing units, relying entirely on the host CPU for compute tasks. Connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reflects strong single-threaded performance, demonstrated by a top-quartile Geekbench single-core score of 2184.0 and strong compression metrics, such as 36.27 GB/sec in gzip single-threaded processing. The server achieved a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3390.33, though uncached large-block read (36.93 GB/sec) and write (19.38 GB/sec) bandwidth fall into the lower percentile tiers. Multi-threaded compute outputs remain stable within the median range, generating a PassMark CPU score of 23271.22 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 10124.0.

This server provides balanced compute density and memory capacity on dedicated single-tenant hardware. Without the overhead of a hypervisor, it is well suited for high-density transactional databases, Redis caching layers, web serving architectures, and software compilation tasks requiring rapid single-core performance coupled with direct NVMe storage access.
description: Vultr vbm-8c-132gb-v2 is a dedicated bare-metal instance powered by an 8-core, 16-thread Intel Xeon E-2388G processor clocked at 3.2 GHz. The platform features 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz and integrates 3840 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, bypassing hypervisor latency for single-tenant workloads. It lacks discrete GPU acceleration, directing all operations to the CPU and its integrated instruction sets, which include AVX-512 and AES-NI. In benchmark evaluations, the server achieves top-quartile single-core metrics, registering a Geekbench single-core score of 2184.0, strong gzip compression speeds of 36.27 GB/sec, and a top-10% PassMark memory score. Multi-threaded processing and cached throughput consistently align with median tier performance. Given its strong single-thread speed, generous RAM-per-core allocation, and substantial NVMe disk, it provides a solid foundation for relational databases, Redis instances, static web serving, and CI/CD compilation tasks.
